topIssues.title: Make post-migration OPCM upgrades work for every chain in an interop set
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The interop migration allows member chains to have different `ProxyAdmin` contracts as long as those contracts have the same L1 ProxyAdmin owner.

During `OPContractsManagerMigrator.migrate`, the shared `ETHLockbox`, `DisputeGameFactory`, and `AnchorStateRegistry` proxies are deployed using the first chain’s `ProxyAdmin`. The first chain’s `DelayedWETH` is also reused by the set. All portals are then pointed at this shared infrastructure.

After migration, `OPContractsManagerV2.upgrade` still assumes that every contract discovered from a chain’s `SystemConfig` is administered by that chain’s `ProxyAdmin`. This is no longer true for chains after the first one.

For example, given two chains with distinct ProxyAdmins owned by the same L1PAO:

```
Portal A admin:       ProxyAdmin A
Portal B admin:       ProxyAdmin B
Shared contract admin: ProxyAdmin A
```

Calling `upgrade()` with Chain B’s `SystemConfig` loads Chain B’s ProxyAdmin along with the shared lockbox, DGF, DelayedWETH, and ASR. `_apply` then attempts to upgrade the shared contracts through ProxyAdmin B.

The common L1PAO passes ProxyAdmin B’s `onlyOwner` check, but the shared proxy only recognizes ProxyAdmin A as its EIP-1967 admin. The shared-contract upgrade therefore reverts, rolling back the entire transaction, including the earlier upgrades to Chain B’s SystemConfig and portal.

As a result, the current `upgrade()` path cannot upgrade the per-chain contracts of every member after an interop migration.

## Desired behavior

Post-migration upgrades should preserve OPCM’s declarative behavior while recognizing that the deployment now contains two resource scopes:

- Per-chain contracts, administered by each chain’s `ProxyAdmin`.
- Shared contracts, administered by the shared infrastructure’s `ProxyAdmin`.

Applying the same desired release repeatedly should be safe and should converge the interop set to the same final state. Existing games, advanced anchors, withdrawal state, balances, and lockbox authorizations must not be reset.

One possible design is to split the existing apply logic into two operations:

- A per-chain apply that upgrades `SystemConfig`, `OptimismPortal`, etc, while preserving and validating the shared contract references.
- A shared apply that upgrades the `ETHLockbox`, DGF, `DelayedWETH`, ASR, and dispute-game configuration exactly once using their actual `ProxyAdmin`.

topIssues.title: op-reth: Provide all command-line args as environment variables
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs

We should make sure that all command-line options can also be set using environment variables.

This improves dev-ops ergonomics and avoids the need for ad-hoc scripts to translate environment variables to command-line options.

Based on this comments https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21551#discussion_r3543956313 and previous discussions with @yashvardhan-kukreja and @geoknee.

topPRs.title: test: reproduce #21663 NUT bundle drift via L2DevFeatureFlags version bump
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Do not merge — diagnostic experiment for the CI failures in ethereum-optimism/optimism#21663.

**What this shows:** the karst/lagoon NUT activation failures come from the **semver downgrade guard** in `L2ContractsManagerUtils.upgradeTo` (reverts `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` when the installed proxy version > the version the bundle installs), combined with a test-fixture gap: **L2DevFeatureFlags is not captured in any pre-fork state file**, so the NUT activation test rebuilds it from HEAD instead of the fork era.

- Before: HEAD L2DevFeatureFlags = 1.0.0, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.0,1.0.0)=false` → pass.
- After the bump: HEAD = 1.0.1, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.1,1.0.0)=true` → downgrade → revert.

Commits:
1. bump L2DevFeatureFlags semver 1.0.0 → 1.0.1
2. comment-only touch to the NUT test file (contracts-only changes don't set `rust_changes_detected`, so the NUT test would be skipped — a CI gap in its own right)
3. regenerate `current-upgrade-bundle.json`
4. regenerate `semver-lock.json`
5. bump the version unit test to 1.0.1 + re-snapshot the **lagoon** bundle (karst left immutable)

Expected CI after commit 5: snapshot checks + version test green; **lagoon** NUT/interop green (bundle now installs 1.0.1, matching HEAD); **karst** NUT still red (its immutable bundle installs 1.0.0 while the test's HEAD genesis has 1.0.1). Note: `nut-provenance-verify lagoon` will fail because the lock commit is the develop merge-base, which predates the change.

topPRs.title: feat: support super-root fault games at initial deployment
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Enforces that initial game types match `SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`. Disabled mode permits `PERMISSIONED_CANNON` and `CANNON_KONA`. Enabled mode permits `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` and `SUPER_CANNON_KONA`. Adds initial `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` support with a `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` fallback. Carries the full starting anchor proposal through Go and Solidity.

**Tests**

Covers both root modes, invalid game types, missing fallbacks, malformed inputs, super-game registration, and anchor propagation.

**Additional context**

OPCM preserves and rejects permissionless requests that do not match its root mode. `FullConfig` does not require a fallback. `DeployOPChain` adds one. Upgrade behavior is unchanged.

**Metadata**

Fixes #21695

topPRs.title: fix(op-revm): discard journal after non-deposit tx errors (SDM warm-set leak)
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`OpHandler::catch_error` reset the EVM journal only on the **deposit** error path. For a **non-deposit** transaction that fails validation (e.g. `NonceTooLow`, or EIP-3607 contract-sender), it returned without calling `journal.discard_tx()`, so the failed tx's partial state — including its **EIP-2929 warm/cold access stamps** — persisted in the shared journal and leaked into the next transaction executed on the same EVM.

On the **SDM `Produce`** execution path (which routes through `inspect_tx`, skipping `finalize()` on error), this means a builder can bill a later included tx a **warm** account access for a tx that never entered the block. A validator re-executing the canonical block (commit-only, `Verify` mode) never ran the skipped tx, recomputes the access as **cold**, and gets a different gas result → **builder-vs-validator divergence → block rejection**.

## Fix

Add the missing `else` branch in `OpHandler::catch_error` calling `journal.discard_tx()` on non-deposit errors, matching upstream revm's `EthHandler::catch_error`. One line of behavior; `rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs`.

This mirrors the same fix independently made upstream in [bluealloy/revm#3780](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/pull/3780) and in Base's EVM fork ([base/base#3806](https://github.com/base/base/pull/3806)). Note that pulling in revm #3780 alone does **not** fix this on the OP path, because `op-revm` overrides `catch_error`.

## Exposure

Not exploitable on chains running today: with SDM disabled (the current production config) execution uses the `transact` path, whose `finalize()` runs even on error and wipes the failed tx's journal. The leak surfaces only once SDM (`Produce` mode) is active.

## Regression coverage

Two layers, both trigger variants (`NonceTooLow` and EIP-3607), each verified **red without the fix** (2500-gas divergence) and **green with it**:

- **`rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/tests.rs`** — builder(`Produce`)-vs-validator(`Verify`) block-executor divergence, plus an SDM-disabled safety guard.
- **`rust/op-rbuilder/.../builders/context.rs`** — the sequencer builder's `execute_best_transactions` selection loop: a skipped failed candidate must not warm a later included tx.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p alloy-op-evm --lib block::tests::sdm::warmleak`
- [x] `cargo test -p op-rbuilder --lib builders::context::tests::skipped`
- [x] Each new test confirmed red against the unfixed handler, green against the fix.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Resolves: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/123
